title: Rabbi Chama ben Lakish
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: So he is cited in the She’iltot, Bereshit, saying: “Whoever answers Amen in this world merits to answer in the world to come.” The statement in Tanchuma, Tzav 9, is attributed to Rabbi Yehudah ben Gadya.

notes.text: פ״צו־ט here denotes parashat Tzav, section 9, rather than a numerical chapter 96. The Buber Tanchuma digital text of Tzav 9 has Yehudah bar Gadya and the Amen saying; the Torat Emet Tanchuma digital text has the parallel at Tzav 7 with Rabbi Yehudah, without that patronymic. Hyman supplies ben Gadya.

The consulted digital She’iltot, Bereshit 1, names Rabbi Chama bar Lakish in this saying about answering Amen in this world and the world to come. Hyman’s heading uses ben Lakish. The Tanchuma comparison above concerns the same saying under another name; these reports do not merge the named figures.
